m0-context.title: Load baseline context
m0-context.imperative: Read the g3 rework handoff in full, the g3 review result, the predecessor implement result, tests/test_episode_negative_control.py, scripts/episode_capture.py, scripts/context_manifest.py, and the engine's CLI flag table. Verify the handoff is complete (task, intent, scope, exclusions, evidence, test mode, stop conditions). Attest c1.

postconditions.statement: handoff + control test + composer + manifest producer + engine flag table read; handoff complete

m1-fix1-argv-census.title: FIX 1 - make `records nothing agent-authored` assert over actual argv
m1-fix1-argv-census.imperative: Record the FULL argv of every issued engine call, then rewrite test_control_records_nothing_agent_authored to assert a closed-world census over those argv: every flag token must be in a per-verb allow-list, every `advance` must carry `--mechanical`, no `attest` may carry `--note`, and the only free-text flag in the entire run must be `reopen --reason` with value == _ControlRun.REOPEN_REASON. State the bounded exception (reopen --reason DOES reach why_trail) in the docstring. Then reproduce reviewer mutation M1 (advance --mechanical -> --why <prose>, plus --note on every attest) and observe the guard RED naming it; restore.

postconditions.statement: M1 red-proof observed: with --why prose on advance and --note on attest, the fixed guard FAILS naming the offending flags (manual attest; a command check would run a by-design-failing test)
guard restored to green over the unmutated control

constraints: do not re-cut the control; do not change --mechanical to --why in the control itself
verify any mutation actually applied by blob OID before trusting its red or its green

m2-fix2-structural-independence.title: FIX 2 - make oracle independence structural, not declarative
m2-fix2-structural-independence.imperative: Rewrite test_every_field_has_a_named_independent_source so independence is proven by EXECUTION (approach a): build the expectations with mechanical_fields, reopen_total, failed_command_count, manifest_ref, _lease_role, _artifact_refs, context_manifest.rev/build_manifest, _ControlRun.compose/snapshot all patched to raise, and reads of the emitted snapshot file blocked. Add an AST-over-code scan as a second layer (approach b) so a module-level from-import cannot dodge the patch. Keep the prose check. Then reproduce reviewer mutation M5 (oracle sources a tally from the composer) and observe RED; restore.

postconditions.statement: M5 red-proof observed: an oracle that reads a tally from the composer FAILS the fixed guard (manual attest)
guard restored to green over the unmutated oracle

constraints: keep the prose check as documentation; it must no longer be the only thing standing

m3-fix3-declared-context-refs.title: FIX 3 - exercise the delivered-context half of the manifest
m3-fix3-declared-context-refs.imperative: Declare real context_refs on the control plan's active gate so a manifest with RESOLVABLE rows is actually produced, and compare those rows per-row against blob OIDs this harness computes itself. Then prove attack A3's condition is REACHABLE: drive the same declaration against absent files and assert deliberately what the control does - rows retained with rev null, and the per-row comparison naming every declared path, so an all-null manifest cannot read as success.

postconditions.statement: a manifest with resolvable declared rows is produced and pasted into the result as evidence (manual attest)
row-level comparison green on the real control and discriminating on the all-null counterfactual

constraints: the counterfactual must run in a temp repo; canon must stay untouched

m4-restore-and-suite.title: Restoration proof and full suite
m4-restore-and-suite.imperative: Prove every mutation restored by blob OID (git hash-object vs git rev-parse HEAD:<path>), confirm git status --porcelain carries nothing but the intended change, and run the full suite accounting for every moved number against the 1485 passed / 2 skipped / 472 subtests baseline.

postconditions.statement: every mutated file's working-tree blob OID equals its HEAD blob OID

check.command: python -c "import subprocess,sys; ps=['scripts/episode_capture.py','scripts/checklist_engine.py','scripts/context_manifest.py']; g=lambda a: subprocess.run(['git']+a,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip(); bad=[p for p in ps if g(['hash-object',p])!=g(['rev-parse','HEAD:'+p])]; print('drifted:',bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

constraints: blob OIDs or normalized content, never raw working-tree bytes (#319)

payload.cmd: python -c "import subprocess,sys; ps=['scripts/episode_capture.py','scripts/checklist_engine.py','scripts/context_manifest.py']; g=lambda a: subprocess.run(['git']+a,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip(); bad=[p for p in ps if g(['hash-object',p])!=g(['rev-parse','HEAD:'+p])]; print('drifted:',bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

why_trail.why: Handoff complete on every field. Confirmed both vacuous guards by reading the code: issued only ever holds argv[0] (line 232), so no flag claim is asserted anywhere; and exp.source is a prose description string, so the forbidden-substring scan checks what the harness SAYS, not what it DOES. Engine flag table read from the argparse block (checklist_engine.py:2301-2397) - advance takes --why/--mechanical/--from-child, attest takes --cond/--which/--note/--evidence, reopen takes a required --reason - which gives a closed-world per-verb flag allow-list for FIX 1.

Closed-world argv census, not a blacklist: ALLOWED_FLAGS is per-verb and any flag outside it fails, so a text-bearing flag the engine grows tomorrow is caught without this file naming it. M1 applied (OID 49059be -> 11a7a01, 9 substitutions, prose visible at 9 call sites) and went RED with 44 violations - per run 7 'advance carries un-sanctioned flag --why', 7 'advance without --mechanical', 4 'attest carries un-sanctioned flag --note', 4 'attest carries --note'. Restored to OID 49059be, 13 passed.

Chose approach (a) - behavioural - because it proves independence by execution and no indirection defeats it. Kept (b) as a second layer for the one hole (a) has: a name bound at import time, which no attribute patch can reach; (b) walks the AST rather than the text so the oracle's own docstring mentioning context_manifest.rev() is not mistaken for a call. Prose check kept as layer (c). M5 arm a (oracle calls episode_capture.reopen_total) RED via (a) and independently reported by (b) as ['episode_capture','reopen_total']; M5 arm b (oracle reads the seam's emitted mechanical/g2.json) RED via the snapshot-read guard. Both restored to OID fb9dfc2.

context_refs declared on BOTH gates (write-if-absent is per-step, so a declaration on only the ending step leaves the other manifest empty). Both topologies now emit files:[{repo,seed.txt,e31de1f3...},{repo,changed_by_the_run.txt,587be6b4...}], compared per row against blob OIDs this harness computes and cross-checked with git hash-object --no-filters. A3 is now reachable: with both declared files absent the rows are RETAINED with rev null, expected_rows() agrees independently, and compare_manifest_rows against a delivered expectation names both paths. context-manifest-ref itself stays correct under A3 because it pins bytes - asserted, not assumed.

No file under scripts/ was ever mutated - both red-proofs were confined to the test file itself, so the safety-classifier workaround was not needed. Restoration proven by blob OID on the mutated file: M1 49059be->11a7a01->49059be (9 substitutions each way), M5a fb9dfc2->d283443->fb9dfc2, M5b fb9dfc2->bd2ef8c->fb9dfc2. All three scripts/ files still equal their HEAD blobs. Suite 1487 passed / 2 skipped / 472 subtests against a 1485/2/472 baseline: +2 is exactly the two tests FIX 3 adds, nothing else moved.
